title: Saved from the fire, Ibrahim and Lut reach a blessed land.
subtitle: Leaving a hostile home for a place of blessing
then: Allah saved Ibrahim from the fire his people lit and {idea}brought him out from among them{/idea}, migrating to the land of Ash-Sham. Lut, who believed in him, went with him. Allah calls it {reward}the land We blessed for the worlds{/reward}.
now: You left the job, the city, or the friend group because staying meant compromising your faith. {trap}It felt like losing everything.{/trap} {reward}Allah can bring you somewhere better than what you left.{/reward}
old: Walking away from a bad place means I end up with less.
new: When I leave something for Allah, He can bring me to something blessed.
try: Thank Allah for one thing you gained after leaving something behind.

title: He asked for one son and was given a grandson too.
subtitle: Ishaq, and Ya'qub as an extra gift
then: Ibrahim had prayed, {idea}my Lord, grant me a righteous son{/idea}. 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd said Allah gave him Ishaq, {reward}and Ya'qub in addition{/reward}. Mujahid said nafilah means a gift. Allah made each of them righteous.
now: You prayed for one job offer and got two. You asked for your child to pass, and he also found good friends. {reward}Allah's answers often come with something extra.{/reward} {idea}Notice the extra.{/idea}
old: I am lucky if Allah gives me exactly what I asked for.
new: Allah answers generously, often with more than I asked.
try: Remember one dua answered with something extra, and thank Allah for the extra.

title: Leaders who guided, prayed, gave, and lived what they taught.
subtitle: Leadership measured by doing good and worship
then: Allah made them {idea}leaders, examples to be followed{/idea}, inviting to Him by His leave. He inspired them to good deeds, prayer, and zakah. The tafsir says {reward}they did what they enjoined others to do{/reward}.
now: At home you tell the kids to put their phones away at dinner while yours is in your hand. {trap}They learn from what you do.{/trap} {idea}You lead your family by living it first.{/idea}
old: Leading means telling others what to do.
new: Real leaders live first what they ask of others.
try: Pick one thing you ask your family to do, and do it yourself today, visibly.

title: Lut was given wisdom and saved from a town of evil.
subtitle: A prophet kept safe among rebellious people
then: Lut believed in Ibrahim, followed him, and migrated with him. Allah {reward}gave him wisdom and knowledge{/reward}, made him a prophet, and sent him to Sodom and its area. {trap}They rejected him{/trap}, and Allah saved him from the town that practised wicked deeds.
now: Your workplace, your building, your online space may make wrong things normal. {trap}It is easy to drift with the place.{/trap} {idea}Lut lived among them and did not become them.{/idea}
old: I am bound to pick up the ways of the place I live.
new: I can live among people and still hold to what is right, with Allah's help.
try: Name one wrong habit normal in your surroundings, and quietly decline it today.

title: Lut was taken into His mercy: one of the righteous.
subtitle: What remains after the town is gone
then: After the story of Lut's people, the verse closes on him: {reward}We admitted him to Our mercy{/reward}. {idea}He was of the righteous.{/idea} The town is not the last word in his story. Mercy is.
now: You feel alone being the one who doesn't laugh at the cruel joke or join the shady deal. {trap}It feels like losing.{/trap} {reward}The last word on the righteous is mercy.{/reward}
old: Standing apart from everyone leaves me with nothing.
new: The righteous end up inside Allah's mercy, even if they stood alone.
try: Ask Allah today: admit me into Your mercy among the righteous.

title: Nuh called out, and he and his family were saved.
subtitle: A dua after centuries of patience
then: Nuh {idea}remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty{/idea}, calling them to Allah, and only a few believed. They plotted against him generation after generation. Then he called on his Lord: I am overcome, so help me. {reward}Allah answered and saved him and those who believed{/reward} from the great distress.
now: You've been trying for years: with a hard relative, a long illness, a child who has drifted. {trap}You feel you have nothing left.{/trap} {idea}Nuh's patience ran for centuries, and then he asked for help.{/idea} {reward}He was answered.{/reward}
old: I have been patient long enough; nothing is changing.
new: Patience and dua go together. Allah answers the one who keeps calling.
try: Make a short, honest dua today: my Lord, I am worn out, so help me.

title: Helped against those who denied, and they were drowned.
subtitle: The end of a people who rejected every sign
then: Allah {reward}saved Nuh and helped him{/reward} against the people who denied His signs. {trap}They were a people given to evil, and Allah drowned them all{/trap}, as their prophet had prayed. The story was told to Makkans who were also mocking a prophet.
now: You are in the minority at the office, at family gatherings, maybe even among friends, on something you know is right. {trap}Numbers feel like proof.{/trap} {idea}Nuh had a few with him, and they were the ones saved.{/idea}
old: If most people disagree with me, I am probably wrong.
new: Numbers do not decide the truth. The few with Nuh were the ones saved.
try: Hold to one right thing today even if you are the only one doing it.

title: Dawud and Sulayman judged the vineyard ruined by sheep at night.
subtitle: Two prophets, one case, and Allah witnessing
then: Ibn Mas'ud said the field was a vineyard whose bunches were spoiled by sheep. {idea}Dawud ruled that the owner of the vineyard should keep the sheep.{/idea} Sulayman proposed another way. Allah says {reward}We were witness to their judgement{/reward}.
now: Your kids fight over a broken toy. Two coworkers bring you a dispute. {trap}You decide quickly to end the noise.{/trap} {idea}Every decision you make between people is witnessed by Allah.{/idea}
old: Sorting out disputes is just about ending the argument.
new: When I judge between people, Allah is witness. Fairness matters, even in small cases.
try: In the next small dispute you settle, listen to both sides fully before deciding.

title: Sulayman was given understanding; both were given wisdom.
subtitle: One saw further, and neither was blamed
then: Sulayman suggested the shepherd tend the vines until they grew back, while the vineyard owner benefited from the sheep, then {reward}each would get his own back{/reward}. Al-Hasan noted that {idea}Allah praised Sulayman but did not condemn Dawud{/idea}. The mountains and birds glorified Allah with Dawud's beautiful recitation.
now: Your colleague's idea turns out better than yours. {trap}You feel small.{/trap} {idea}Sincere effort is honoured even when someone else sees further.{/idea} {reward}Learn from it, without shame.{/reward}
old: If my judgment turns out wrong, I have failed.
new: Sincere effort is honoured. I can learn from a better answer without shame.
try: Tell someone today that their idea was better than yours, and mean it.

title: Dawud was taught to make armor. Will you be grateful?
subtitle: A skill taught by Allah, for people's protection
then: Qatadah said people used to wear plated armor, and Dawud {reward}was the first to make rings of chain mail{/reward}. The tafsir says Allah blessed people when He inspired His servant Dawud and taught him this for their sake. {idea}Are you then grateful?{/idea}
now: You are good at code, at nursing, at fixing cars, at calming a crying baby. {trap}It feels like it is just you.{/trap} {reward}Every skill is something Allah taught{/reward}, and it is meant to protect and help others.
old: My skills are mine; I earned them.
new: My skills were taught to me by Allah. Gratitude is using them for good.
try: Use one of your skills today to help someone, for free.

title: The strong wind ran at Sulayman's command, by Allah's leave.
subtitle: Power over nature, given and known by Allah
then: The tafsir introduces this as {reward}the unparalleled power of Sulayman{/reward}: Allah subjugated the strong wind to him, running by his command toward the land Allah had blessed. The verse ends: {idea}of all things We are Knowing{/idea}.
now: You have power you take for granted: a car, a salary, a team that answers to you. {trap}It can start to feel like yours.{/trap} {idea}Every bit of control you have is lent, and Allah knows how you use it.{/idea}
old: The control I have over my life is my own doing.
new: Any power I hold is subjected to me by Allah, and He knows how I use it.
try: Use one bit of authority you have today more gently than usual.

title: Even devils worked for Sulayman, and Allah kept them in check.
subtitle: No force works outside Allah's guard
then: Among the devils were some {idea}who dived for Sulayman and did other work{/idea}. Allah says {reward}it was We who guarded them{/reward}. Even the most rebellious creatures worked only within His control.
now: You feel at the mercy of things you can't see: whispers, bad luck, other people's envy. {trap}Fear can make them feel huge.{/trap} {idea}Nothing in the unseen works outside Allah's guard.{/idea}
old: There are dark forces out there I cannot do anything about.
new: Even the devils are under Allah's control. I seek refuge in Him and move on.
try: Recite Ayat al-Kursi tonight before sleep, and leave the fear with Allah.

title: Ayyub said: harm has touched me, and You are most merciful.
subtitle: A dua that names the pain and the mercy
then: Ayyub had livestock, crops, many children and fine houses, and {trap}lost them all{/trap}. Then his body was tested, and only his wife cared for him. The Prophet ﷺ said the prophets are tested most severely. Ayyub {reward}had the utmost patience{/reward}, and his dua names only the harm and Allah's mercy.
now: Lying awake in the hospital bed, or after the business went under, you want to ask why me. {idea}Ayyub simply told Allah it hurt, and called Him the Most Merciful.{/idea} {reward}That is patience and honesty together.{/reward}
old: Being patient means never saying it hurts.
new: I can tell Allah it hurts and still call Him the Most Merciful. That is patience.
try: In your next dua, tell Allah plainly what hurts, then call Him Arham ar-Rahimin.

title: He was answered: healed, his family restored, and as many again.
subtitle: Ayyub's story as a reminder for anyone tested
then: Allah removed his distress and {reward}restored his family and the like of them{/reward}, as a mercy. The tafsir says Allah made him an example {idea}lest those beset by trials think it is because He does not care for them{/idea}. When healed, Ayyub said: who can ever have enough of Your mercy?
now: A long hard year makes you wonder if Allah has forgotten you. {trap}That thought is exactly what this story answers.{/trap} {idea}Ayyub's test was a sign of his rank, and it ended in mercy.{/idea}
old: If I am being tested this hard, Allah must not care about me.
new: Trials are not a sign that Allah doesn't care. Ayyub's ended in mercy.
try: Write down one hard time that ended. Read it the next time you feel forgotten.
